item.title: Artificial Intelligence and Human Consciousness
item.author: hari@dasarpai.com (Dr. Hari Thapliyaal)
item.description:
Artificial Intelligence and Human Consciousness
#

A teenage girl stood on a table at a large conference and spoke about the dangers of artificial intelligence. I do not know her full story, or the full setting. What stayed was not the table. It was the question under her words.

Are we conscious of the consequences of what we are creating?

item.title: Three Types of People
item.author: hari@dasarpai.com (Dr. Hari Thapliyaal)
item.description:
Three Types of People
#

In our personal, social, political, and spiritual lives, there are broadly three kinds of people.

These levels are not fixed. They change from situation to situation, and from one part of life to another. The same person can be the first kind at work, the second kind in politics, and the third kind in faith. Each kind meets suffering and joy in a different way.

item.title: The Nature, Power, and Limits of Systems
item.author: hari@dasarpai.com (Dr. Hari Thapliyaal)
item.description:
The Nature, Power, and Limits of Systems
#

To do more than one person can do alone, people create systems.

A system turns resources into power
#

A family, company, political party, government, military, religious organization, university, hospital, cooperative, social movement, or village community can all become a system. Each system gathers resources: money, people, knowledge, land, technology, authority, reputation, infrastructure, relationships, and experience.

item.title: Who Is Our Enemy?
item.author: hari@dasarpai.com (Dr. Hari Thapliyaal)
item.description:
Who Is Our Enemy?
#

We use the words friend and enemy very easily.

Someone supports what I want to do:

He is my friend.

Someone opposes me:

He is my enemy.

Someone remains silent when I expect support:

He is not really my friend.

But is it so simple?

item.title: Sign of Wisdom
item.author: hari@dasarpai.com (Dr. Hari Thapliyaal)
item.description:
Sign of Wisdom
#

Your surroundings comprise people, lives,
the government, and systems around you,
including family members, office hierarchy,
political setup, religious teachings, elders, youth,
colleagues, even other lives like pets or animals nearby.

Your relationship with the surroundings is influenced by them.
You aren’t entirely responsible for creating a harmonious atmosphere.
Some people are generally good but hostile towards you,
Some are naturally hostile;
If you attempt to change them against their will,
You’ll waste your life, time, and energy.
Changing systems, religious beliefs, and
government is an extremely daunting task.
In human history, those who changed their surroundings
didn’t do it by changing others,
but by changing themselves.

item.title: Four Kinds of Powers of a Society
item.author: hari@dasarpai.com (Dr. Hari Thapliyaal)
item.description:
Four Kinds of Powers of a Society
#

Whether you appreciate this or not, ancient Indian wisdom says the following.
If you are constantly losing intellectual debate, narrative then Brahminhood of your society is in danger.
If you are constantly losing physical fights with enemies then Kshatruyahood of the society is in danger.
If you are constantly losing trade to other countries or societies then Vaisyahood of the society is in danger.
If you are constantly producing substandard skills of your workforce to support your own three pillars and societies then your shoodrahood is in danger.

item.title: Human Peace
item.author: hari@dasarpai.com (Dr. Hari Thapliyaal)
item.description:
Human Peace
#

Information has become abundant
and it is free through search engines like Google, bing, yahoo etc.

Knowledge has become abundant
and free through Wikipedia, quora etc.

Energy is becoming abundant through nuclear, wind, solar, etc.

Communication has become abundant
through new mobile communication technologies.

Entertainment has become abundant through YouTube, netflix, imdb, etc.
